ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard capture of a high‑energy October ’71 show highlighted by a stunning “Comes A Time” and tight, rock‑driven renditions.
ai_review.review: The recording is praised for its crystal‑clear soundboard source, with the new Keith Godchaux’s bright piano sitting front‑and‑center and Jerry’s vocals described as chillingly beautiful. The performance is energetic and focused – “Comes A Time”, the Not Fade Away / Goin’ Down The Road sequence, Jack Straw and Tennessee Jed receive repeated accolades, while a few listeners note the shorter jams typical of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive comments on both musical performance and audio fidelity (majority 5‑star reviews, detailed praise of sound quality and standout songs).

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clean, clear mix; occasional mention of the source being obvious in the GDTRFB segment but not detracting. Consistently described as “great sounding”, “crisp” and superior to older analog copies.

standout_songs: Not Fade Away > Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad
show_quality.setlist_flow: Melodic and focused set with inventive short jams; tight transitions and engaging banter keep momentum despite the era’s generally shorter improvisations.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as chilling, peak of his vocal abilities, harmonizing with Bob on several tunes, and delivering emotive falsetto on “Comes A Time”.
band_member_comments.Phil: Praised for wonderful bass work; occasional mention of “Phil bombs” style playing.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for strong harmonies with Jerry on “Me and Bobby McGee” and “Jack Straw”.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux’s debut highlighted – bright, upfront, rock‑in’ piano that fits in after only a short rehearsal period.
